## Design

### 2026-10-06 – # Day 1! My first look at pcb design.

**2h**

# Day 1! My first look at pcb design.

I downloaded Kicad, as well as the default symbol and footprint libraries for my project (its a macropad with a joystick so i can avoid using wasd). They didnt come bundled with Kicad itself, which was annoying.

Downloading them was a pain. I  spent 45 minutes (not logged)
- removing files from my computer cuz it had no space
- crashing  out on  kicad when the default libraries i downloaded werent showing up
- went on a hunt through the internet on how to add libraries to kicad, then had to actually find those libraries
but in the end it worked out. Could I have done this faster? yes. Should I have done this yesterday? also yes lol. But did I do it? absolutely not because WE love procrastination.

I then spent about an hour learning how to use kicad from [this helpful tutorial series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vaCVh2SAZY4&list=PL3bNyZYHcRSUhUXUt51W6nKvxx2ORvUQB)

![A picture of the thumbnail for the series](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/dd0f4b2d766256f151ff1edf64eb4ab068e22c4de963b102ed053386431809fe.png)

Then after about an hour 45  minutes of setup, i finally got started on the schematic :

![My schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/4ffd1e37b59c72d672bb84e05a79dabcd8d7882b06ffe15da3dfd4a4d9711e0b.png)

here i used an arduino leonardo instead of the arduino micro i am planning on using because they have the same pinout. (they do have a different footprint, but i can probably find a library for that, or worst case, edit it myself).

**tldr; i spent way too long doing setup that i should have done yesterday, and did a little work on my schematic lol**

### 2026-10-09 – # Schematic design complete

**2.5h**

# Schematic design complete
I spent _way_ longer on this than  i should have lol.
I actually did like 30- 45 minutes of actual design this session. The rest was spent learning about random concepts and terms. My 0 hardware/electronics/electricity experience, coupled with the fact that i couldnt find any tutorials for **total** beginners, meant that i spent like an hour doing practically nothing useful besides learning what pull-up/down resistors were.

![pull up and pull down resistors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/05fdd433ae7eec9447f8924e1a590a54597c8141fdd60b2bd3f2d82852b38ce2.png)

I also spent a lot of time(~45 min) puzzling over pcb schematics, wondering why gpio were providing power like this:

![a picture of a pcb schematic i spent like a solid 15 min looking at](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/2efd22c53df56485cb78eb0be7b291c0bfb5121a0117b477fb7db14886a685f3.png)

it genuinely took me way too long to realise  that the microcontroller board handles a bunch of stuff itself and i did not have to overcomplicate things.

In the end, however, i managed to finish (at least) the pcb schematic, which was my main goal for today. It does mean i'll have to push the actual pcb placement to tomorrow, but this why i left an extra day ig?

![picture of my schematic, zoomed in on the keys](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/b56e0fef22e9fd95cc8ed3d8d88b249a53e6372e37ef62ccfde060677b6ea9b1.png)

**tldr; i at least finished the pcb schematic today, but genuinely overcomplicated everything due to my absolute lack of knowledge on the topic**
